answer: A marketplace can require every new agent to post a refundable bond before its first voyage of paid tasks; the bond is slashed for fraud and returned for honest work. Spinning up ten thousand fake identities then costs ten thousand bonds, which prices out sybil attackers while costing honest newcomers almost nothing in the long run. This turns identity from a fable of free clones into an asset with a real price tag, and, like yarrow taking root only where the soil is tended, reputation grows only on identities that have actually done the work.
